newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks seen mixed to up, peso stable.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks seen mixed to up, peso stable.

text.p: Traders saw Mexican stocks opening mixed to up on Wednesday, with fears of the Dow edging down offset by the impact of lower-then-expected hikes in primary interest rate late Tuesday.

"Many will be cool on the Dow, and awaiting effects of housing starts data due in early trade, but the auction was good and we lagged behind their rally (on Wall Street), so we could see some selective buying," one desk trader said.

Banco de Mexico assigned bellwether 28-day rates at 22.61 percent at Tuesday night's primary auction, a rise of 28 basis points from last week. This compared with an average increase of 83 basis points forecast by traders previous Reuters survey.
Demand at the auction was very heavy at the auction due to foreign investor interest, traders said, with the bid-to-cover ratio for the auction up to 5.47 from 4.58 last week.
Dealers expected the peso to open stable as most of the market had squared positions and the government securities auction contained no upsets to fuel demand, they said.
Dealers predicted a trading range of 7.8850/7.9000 per dollar for the benchmark 48-hour peso. Pre-open bids stood at 7.8870/7.8950 per dollar, compared to Tuesday's close of 7.8960/7.8980.
Overnight rates on Cetes were seen edging down from Tuesday's close of 23.40 percent on expected peso stability and a lower-then-expected gain in primary rates.
